name: Salutations
overview: Scripture reveals that salutations in biblical times were expressions of respect and honor, often demonstrated through physical gestures such as bowing deeply to the ground, as Abraham and Lot did when meeting others (Genesis 18:2; 19:1; 23:7). These acts of reverence extended to addressing others with titles of respect, like 'my lords,' reflecting recognition of authority and hospitality (Genesis 19:2). The repeated bowing of Jacob before his brother emphasizes humility and reconciliation within family relationships (Genesis 33:3), illustrating salutations as both social and spiritual gestures grounded in honor and peace.
